stories.summary: Verify the host audit chain and expose chain verification as a read tool
stories.description: verify_audit_chain exists but nothing calls it, and the host chain (.audit.host.jsonl) has no verifier at all.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83 - a stand-in of AA-01 and AA-02 together (shared chain verifier, verify_audit in the lifecycle TOOLS tuple and REMOTE_READ, pipeline/audit_anchor.py wired into scan_all_plans, the doc lines): first run 2 conflicts - tests/unit/test_lifecycle_tool_registration.py::test_tools_tuple_has_nine_entries_in_original_order (exact TOOLS enumeration; pre-authorized in AA-01) and tests/unit/test_readme_reference_split.py::test_moved_section_body_is_verbatim[MCP tools reference] (re-scoped: the tool is documented in the Audit stream section instead). Re-run with both resolutions: 17749 passed / 21 skipped, 0 conflicts. Four other failures are environment-only and fail identically on untouched master in the planning container (test_aider_harness_availability x2: proxy-injected GH_TOKEN; test_docs_have_no_personal_home_path: the container HOME is the root user's home, which the guard bans by value; test_remote_sync ssh: no ssh binary).

TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHY: pipeline/audit.py defines `verify_audit_chain(plan_name)` but no tool, route or CLI calls it, and the host-scoped chain written by `append_host_audit` (remote MCP authentication attempts, host config writes) has no verifier.

WHAT TO BUILD:
1. pipeline/audit.py: extract the loop of `verify_audit_chain` into `_verify_chain_at(path) -> int | None` (same semantics: the seq of the first bad line, or None when intact); `verify_audit_chain(plan_name)` delegates to it; add `verify_host_audit_chain() -> int | None` over `_host_audit_path()`.
2. A read-only MCP tool `verify_audit`, defined in pipeline/server_tools_lifecycle.py and appended as the LAST entry of its `TOOLS` tuple (pipeline/server.py registers that tuple in a loop; server.py is capped at 994 lines by tests/unit/test_lifecycle_tool_registration.py - do not add lines there) returning `{"ok": True, "plans": {<plan>: None | <bad seq>}, "host": None | <bad seq>}` for every plan with an audit file. Add it to `REMOTE_READ` in pipeline/remote_tool_policy.py (read-only). Membership assertions only for both registries.

AUTHORIZED EDITS TO EXISTING TESTS (exactly these): tests/unit/test_lifecycle_tool_registration.py - append `"verify_audit",` as the last element of `EXPECTED_TOOL_NAMES` (after `"reject_plan",`), and change `assert len(lifecycle.TOOLS) == 11` to `assert len(lifecycle.TOOLS) == 12`, updating the comment above it to say AA-01 appended `verify_audit`. Justification for the commit body: that test pins registration order on purpose and was extended the same way when ENT-LC-02b appended the plan-approval tools.

DOCS: do NOT add a bullet to REFERENCE.md's `## MCP tools reference` section - tests/unit/test_readme_reference_split.py compares it byte-for-byte. Instead document `verify_audit` (and the host chain) in REFERENCE.md's `### Audit stream (PIPELINE_PLAN_DIR/<plan>.audit.jsonl)` subsection, right after the sentence ending "or `None` when the stream is intact."; and in the Remote MCP transport section change "six read-only tools" to "seven read-only tools" and add `verify_audit` to that list. docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md "Audit stream" (host chain now verified).

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_audit_verify_tool.py): intact chains report None; an edited middle line reports its seq for a plan chain and for the host chain; a deleted middle line is detected; an empty/missing file is intact; the tool is registered and in REMOTE_READ; truncating the tail is NOT detected (document the limit with a test named for it - AA-02 closes it).

GENERAL RULES (every step of this story):
- Write the failing tests first (CLAUDE.md Step 3) and confirm they fail on an assertion, not an import error.
- Verify with the full suite `.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q` AND `.venv/bin/python -m ruff check .` AND `.venv/bin/python scripts/check_line_limit.py`; all must be green before you finish. Report pass/fail counts in the PR description.
- A new test file that imports any `pipeline.*` module must `import pipeline.server` first (pre-existing import cycle). Copy the idiom in tests/unit/test_triage_cap_silent_skip.py.
- Bind a non-operator principal in tests the way tests/unit/test_patch_plan_enforcement.py does (`pipeline.actor.bind_principal`); never add an `actor` parameter to any MCP tool (a guard test forbids it).
- The harness scratchpad `.agent_scratchpad.md` stays untracked. Commit only the files this brief names plus the new test files it asks for. Add no helper scripts, dumps or module copies.
- Never modify an existing test except as this brief pre-authorizes, with the literal edit given. If another pre-existing test fails because of a change this brief requires, do NOT undo the required change - stop and report the conflict, naming the test and the requirement it contradicts.
- Comments and docs you write must stay true after later stories merge: state the invariant, never "until story X lands".
- Cumulative artifacts (the REFERENCE.md policy table, the IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md section 4 rows, `REMOTE_*` sets): assert only what YOU add or remove (membership/absence), never the full contents, an exact count, or a hash.
- Error messages and logs name the action and the principal subject only - never a token, secret, payload, path or exception text (Secure-by-Design).
- Commit message: Conventional Commits (`<type>(<scope>): <subject>`, subject <=72 chars), body explains why; put the story key in the body. If you change an existing test as pre-authorized, the body must say which test and why (CLAUDE.md Step 4).

stories.summary: Anchor audit chain heads outside PLAN_DIR so tail truncation is detectable
stories.description: The hash chain proves order, not completeness: deleting the last N lines leaves a valid chain. Periodically write each chain's head to an anchor sink and verify against it.
stories.agent_instructions:
Preflight: impact run 2026-10-28 on master cd09a83 - a stand-in of AA-01 and AA-02 together (shared chain verifier, verify_audit in the lifecycle TOOLS tuple and REMOTE_READ, pipeline/audit_anchor.py wired into scan_all_plans, the doc lines): first run 2 conflicts (both AA-01's) - tests/unit/test_lifecycle_tool_registration.py::test_tools_tuple_has_nine_entries_in_original_order (exact TOOLS enumeration; pre-authorized in AA-01) and tests/unit/test_readme_reference_split.py::test_moved_section_body_is_verbatim[MCP tools reference] (re-scoped: the tool is documented in the Audit stream section instead). TARGET IMPLEMENTER: cloud open-source (Claude-class sizing, every mechanically checkable requirement graded below). Provider/model are NOT pinned: dispatch resolves them from the live model registry's `roles.dispatch` entry.

WHAT TO BUILD (new module pipeline/audit_anchor.py, at most 3 new public functions):
1. `PIPELINE_AUDIT_ANCHOR`: unset/empty = off (today's behavior); `file:<absolute path>` = append-only JSONL anchor log; anything else (unknown scheme, relative path, a path inside PLAN_DIR) raises `ValueError` at first use with a message naming the variable, never the value of any secret. Fail closed, ADR 0004.
2. `anchor_heads()`: for every plan chain and the host chain, append `{"chain": <plan|"host">, "seq": <head seq>, "hash": <head hash>, "at": <utc iso>}` when the head changed since the last anchor for that chain. Open with O_APPEND; never rewrite the file.
3. `verify_against_anchor(chain) -> str | None`: None when the chain still contains the anchored (seq, hash); else a reason ("truncated below anchored seq N", "anchored hash mismatch at seq N").
4. Wire `anchor_heads()` into `pipeline/watchers.py` `scan_all_plans` (runs every daemon tick), guarded so a sink error logs a WARNING with the error type only and never stops the scan (catching `Exception` there needs `# noqa: BLE001 - <reason>`, the convention used across pipeline/, because the handler logs a WARNING rather than calling `logger.exception`); and extend AA-01's `verify_audit` result with an `anchor` entry per chain when anchoring is on.

The `file:` sink only helps if the path is on storage the pipeline host cannot rewrite (a WORM/object-lock mount, a separate host's NFS export with append-only permissions). Say so in the docs; an HTTP/S3 sink is a later story.

DOCS: REFERENCE.md configuration table row for `PIPELINE_AUDIT_ANCHOR`; docs/specs/IDENTITY_AND_POLICY.md "Audit stream durability" row; docs/plans/ENTERPRISE_PLATFORM_READINESS.md Auditability verdict.

TESTS (new tests/unit/test_audit_anchor.py): off by default writes nothing; anchors once per changed head (two ticks with no change -> one line); truncating the tail after an anchor is detected; editing the anchored line is detected; a path inside PLAN_DIR, a relative path and an unknown scheme each raise; a sink write failure does not stop scan_all_plans.
